>
[Boastful Hunter](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1178)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 162

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 or 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Jezail](/Weapons.aspx?ID=203)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +11; precise vision 30 feet, imprecise hearing 30 feet

**Communication** speech ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1))

**Skills** [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +9, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +10, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +11

**Int** +0, **Wis** +2, **Cha** +3

**Will** +11 

</column>

---        

Possessing a boisterous, proud demeanor, this _+1 [jezail](/Weapons.aspx?ID=203)_ is an aspiring big game hunter, always quick to share a tale of its bold adventures and predatory conquests—although the veracity of such tales is often questionable. A _boastful hunter_ enjoys tracking and hunting animals of all kinds but takes particular pleasure in taking down large, dangerous, or rare animals. Against an [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9), the _boastful hunter_ deals 1d6 additional damage. On a critical hit against an animal, the _boastful hunter_ also deals 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

 A _boastful hunter_ urges you to face off against tougher and tougher creatures—a challenge the ambitious rifle may not be adequate to deal with. If the _boastful hunter_ goes one week without participating in a hunt against an animal of at least your level, it becomes bored. A bored _boastful hunter_ complains incessantly and imposes a –1 item penalty to attack rolls against non-animal targets. A bored _boastful hunter_ can be appeased by using it in combat against an animal of at least your level.

 Unable to accept its own weaknesses, a _boastful hunter_ blames any failed hunts on you, and considers remarks about its strength or quality a terrible insult. An insulted _boastful hunter_ badmouths you to sentient creatures you interact with, imposing a –1 item penalty to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) skill checks, and all attacks with it incur a misfire chance until the weapon is appeased. An insulted _boastful hunter_ can be appeased by complimenting it and succeeding at a Diplomacy check against its Will DC two days in a row. You can only attempt a Diplomacy check to appease the _boastful hunter_ once each day.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Body Recovery Kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=840)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 26

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Players can gain access to faction-specific gear by taking the corresponding Faction Gear Access Game Reward, available when they reach 20 reputation with the respective faction._

**Price** 101 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Membership in the Envoy's Alliance Pathfinder Society faction.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This small silver tin is filled with a herb-infused salve and a shroud of fine silk fabric. The salve smells of lavender and hyssop and is waxy to the touch. The shroud, made of spun silk, can a hold a Medium or smaller creature. If you apply the salve and shroud to a creature that died within the past 3 days, a process which normally takes 1 hour, it slows the decomposition process, allowing a creature to be brought back to life with raise dead up to 1 week after its death.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 63

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This apparatus increases the viscosity of the reagents in alchemical bombs, to deadly effect. As a 10-minute activity that has the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait, you can use a bomb coagulant alembic to distill the contents of one [infused](/Traits.aspx?ID=797) alchemical bomb that deals [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage into a stickier substance. After distilling, the bomb deals no splash damage but instead deals [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) equal to and of the same type as its original splash damage. If the bomb already deals persistent damage, distilling increases that damage by the bomb’s original splash damage.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 64

**Price** 20 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This long, hollow tube is held in two hands and braced over the shoulder. Inside, it contains a small metal basket sized to hold [alchemical bombs](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=7). A chute in the top delivers an alchemical bomb into the internal basket, while a lever on the underside pulls the basket back and locks it in place. Loading an alchemical bomb into a bomb launcher requires a single Interact action. With a pull of a trigger, the basket speeds forward, allowing you to Strike with the loaded alchemical bomb over long distances. Bombs fired with a bomb launcher have a [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of 60 feet.

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 589 **Price** 75 gp --- You create a snare that catalyzes three 3rd-level moderate [alchemical bombs](/Equipment.aspx?Category=7) of the same type to explode when a creature enters the snare’s square. The target and all creatures in adjacent squares must attempt a DC 26 Reflex save, as the snare deals damage equal to three times the direct hit damage from one of the component bombs (for example, 6d6 electricity damage from [bottled lightning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=76)) with no splash damage or other effects. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and no other effects.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage. It also takes all other effects of a direct hit from one of the component bombs (such as flat-footed from bottled lightning or persistent damage from an [acid flask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=74)).
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage, plus all other effects of a direct hit (as failure). **Craft Requirements** Supply three of the same damaging 3rd-level moderate alchemical bomb.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 13"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Bomber's Saddle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=657)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Companion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=29" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands](/Sources.aspx?ID=33) pg. 76

**Price** 2,800 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn saddle

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Developed by [urdefhans](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=158) for their [skaveling](/Monsters.aspx?ID=803) mounts but quickly copied by other races' cavalry, this leather saddle is made from [cave worm](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=21) hide and is designed to fit a variety of flying steeds. In addition to a seat for the rider, the _bomber's saddle_ has a bomb compartment situated underneath the mount. The compartment can hold up to six [alchemical bombs](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=7) of light or negligible Bulk.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You drop a single item from the saddle's compartment, which falls to the ground below. If the item is a [bomb](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=2), make a ranged Strike with it.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;    **Requirements** The saddle's compartment is loaded with two to six bombs; **Effect** You drop the saddle's entire payload, scattering the bombs below. Make a single ranged Strike against an AC of 10. The AC increases by 1 for every 5 feet above the target area you are. On a failure, the bombs fly away wildly and deal no damage. On a successful attack roll, the bombs fall and shatter, starting in the target area and moving in a line of 5-foot spaces up to 30 feet long for six bombs, one bomb per space. The bombs don't directly hit any creatures; instead, creatures take [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage from the bombs as usual, but combine the splash damage from multiple overlapping bombs together before applying weaknesses or resistances. Apply any effects normally applied to splash damage when throwing a bomb (such as the effects of the [Calculated Splash](/Feats.aspx?ID=99) feat).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Bone Dreadnought Plate](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1974)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 63

**Price** 1,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 5
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Fortress Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=21)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This suit of bone-based [fortress plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=21) is a masterpiece of alchemical science. This armor has a receiver that can hold a single [lodestone bomb](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1904), which takes 3 Interact actions to install.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** A lodgestone bomb is installed in the armor; **Effect** The bomb shifts numerous small plates and hinges, offering a wide variety of protections, granting you resistance to [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), piercing, and slashing damage equal to the loaded lodestone bomb’s splash damage. These effects last for 20 minutes, but each time you’re hit by an attack that deals damage of one of these types, decrease the remaining duration by 1 minute. Once activated, the armor can’t be deactivated. The activation uses up the lodestone bomb, and the armor can’t be activated again until a new one is installed.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 10 Bone Dreadnought Plate Alchemical Source Treasure Vault pg. 63 Price 1,000 gp Usage worn armor Bulk 5 Base Armor Fortress Plate Activate Single Action Interact This suit of bone-based fortress plate is a masterpiece of alchemical science. This armor has a receiver that can hold a single lodestone bomb, which takes 3 Interact actions to install. A loaded suit of bone dreadnought plate can be activated to cause the bomb to shift numerous small plates and hinges, offering a wide variety of protections, granting you resistance to cold, electricity, fire, piercing, and slashing damage equal to the loaded lodestone bomb’s splash damage. These effects last for 20 minutes, but each time you’re hit by an attack that deals damage of one of these types, decrease the remaining duration by 1 minute. Once activated, the armor can’t be deactivated. The armor uses up the lodestone bomb during the duration and can’t be activated again until a new one is installed.

A _bonebloom rose_ appears as a blue-petaled rose, often found growing within the ribs of a skeleton buried in a grave under Pharasma’s protection. These consumable items can also be crafted as any other item. When you activate a _bonebloom rose_, you inhale deeply from its petals while squeezing the stem hard enough that its thorns painfully (but otherwise harmlessly) pierce your flesh. The rose then withers and crumbles to dust, and you gain 40 temporary Hit Points for 1 hour. As long as you have at least 1 of these temporary Hit Points remaining (and they haven’t been replaced by temporary Hit Points from a different source), your Strikes deal an additional 2 spirit damage to undead.

This small, opalescent stone glows with a light that constantly shifts between colors. When you activate the stone, you throw it into a space within 100 feet. The stone then casts [_dimension door_](/Spells.aspx?ID=69) on you and transports you to itself. This destroys the stone.

 You can instead hurl the stone at a creature in an attempt to bring that creature closer to you. Make a ranged Strike against a creature using your highest proficiency with a ranged weapon. The swapping stone has a [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of 15 feet. On a hit, the stone shatters against the creature, casting _dimension door_ on the creature and causing it to instantly teleport to a space adjacent to you. An unwilling creature can resist this teleportation with a successful DC 28 Will save.

Touching the book causes a sense of faint discombobulation. **Activate—Bewildering Walls** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** If your next action is to [Cast a prepared Wall Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734), such as _[_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1748)_ or _[_wall of thorns_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1752)_, you imbue the wall with an uncanny sense of disorientation, causing creatures to perceive it as an endless labyrinth. Regardless of the results, the target then becomes immune to Bewildering Walls for 24 hours. **Critical Success** The wall has no additional effect for that creature.
**Success** The creature is bewildered by its perceptions of labyrinthine walls and treats all other creatures as [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature treats all other creatures as [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature treats all other creatures as hidden for 1 round and concealed for 1 minute.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 15"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Book of Lost Days](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1640)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 160

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This massive tome's yellowed pages curl at the edges, and the letters on its face and spine are too worn to be read. When you open the book, it always opens to a page that seems to perfectly answer the question you had in mind, but reading more than a few lines causes your head to swim alarmingly.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 hour (envision, Interact);    **Requirements** You aren't [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10); **Effect** You open the book while trying to learn information about any topic. The _Book of Lost Days_ permits you to view another's memory, which contains information about that subject commensurate to rolling a total of 40 to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about the topic, with additional context provided on a success or critical success.

 The price for this knowledge is the memory of a day in your past, and the vitality of a day in your future. You lose the memory of that day completely, and the total of all the knowledge you learned on that date is added to the book's repository of information. The book, not you, chooses which memories are taken, preferring days with concentrated emotional resonance, and thus tends to steal significant life moments. This loss affects only your memories; it has no effect on your level, class, feats, or other character choices.

 Your natural lifespan is also shortened by 1 day. The loss of this life energy causes you to be drained 2. You can't reduce the drained condition for 2 days, after which you can recover normally from the condition.

 Creatures have occasionally managed to use the _Book of Lost Days_ not to gain others' knowledge but to wipe their minds clean of painful memories or deadly secrets. Their memories aren't destroyed but merely stored in the book, where someone else might later retrieve them.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 92

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The book is leather-bound and decorated with the symbol of the Lantern Lodge. Red and gold cords wrap around the book and tie to keep it shut. Each volume offers translation for a different language. When working with a book of translation, you can attempt [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) or to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) with creatures that speak the language featured in the book, even if you do not speak the language. Such checks take 10 times longer to complete and you take a –2 circumstance penalty to the check due to your limited communication capabilities.

fields.text: Item 8 Book of Warding Prayers Divine Grimoire Transmutation Source Treasure Vault pg. 111 Price 425 gp Bulk L Script in a language of the Outer Planes adorns this book’s spine, and a deity’s symbol is etched on its cover. Books of warding prayers are each devoted to a particular deity and are also a religious symbol of that deity. Activate Free Action envision; Frequency once per day; Trigger Your last action was to cast a prepared divine spell granted by your deity; Effect Choose chaotic, evil, good, or lawful; you can’t choose a type that’s part of your deity’s alignment. You and all allies within 30 feet are suffused with your deity’s protection, gaining resistance 10 to damage of that type for 1 minute.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 1"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Bookthief Brew](/Equipment.aspx?ID=844)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 30

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Players can gain access to faction-specific gear by taking the corresponding Faction Gear Access Game Reward, available when they reach 20 reputation with the respective faction._

**Price** 3 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Member of the Pathfinder Society.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row>1 minute (Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This concoction mixes into a thick, paste-like substance when shaken. When exposed to air, the substance dries after one minute. If poured over a book, scroll, or other material featuring words written in ink, the brew will make an exact copy of the words it is in contact with while it dries, though it doesn't contain any magical effect or other special properties of the original words. Once dried, you can remove the dried substance as an Interact action. A single vial of bookthief brew can coat two pages from a book, a single scroll, or a similar amount of area for other surfaces, producing a dried sheet as thick as a piece of paper. Unfortunately, the sheet's copy is flipped, requiring a mirror to properly read.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

**Price** 18 gp

---

By combining a [lesser alchemist's fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=75), a [ lesser thunderstone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=79), and other catalysts with a pressure sensitive trigger, you create a snare that creates a fiery and thunderous explosion when triggered. The target and all creatures in adjacent squares take 2d6 fire damage and 2d6 sonic damage with a basic DC 19 Reflex save. On a failure, they are deafened for 1d4 rounds and take 1d4 persistent fire damage.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a [lesser alchemist's fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=75) and a [ lesser thunderstone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=79).

On a failure, the target is also [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) for 1 round.

The springy soles of these sturdy leather boots cushion your feet and make each step lighter. These boots give you a +5- foot item bonus to your Speed and a +2 item bonus to Athletics checks to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36) and [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37). In addition, when you use the Leap action, you can move 5 feet further if jumping horizontally or 3 feet higher if jumping vertically.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />

These boots act as [_greater boots of elvenkind_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=413), but they react wildly to strong physical exertion. While you wear the boots, the curse activates whenever you attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check or Stride more than once in a single round during an encounter. The boots cast an 8th-level [_uncontrollable dance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=347) spell on you, and you automatically fail your save. Once the curse has activated for the first time, the boots fuse to you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Boots of Free Running](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2456)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 84

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** 1
</row>

**Access** Second-mark members of the Firebrands have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These comfortable and practical boots slip on easily and fill you with boundless energy. The treads of these boots provide exceptional traction, with improved grip on surfaces you would traditionally have difficulty traversing. While wearing the boots, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28) and to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36) and [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The traction of your boots improves, allowing you to run along vertical surfaces for 1 minute. When you Stride, you can run up solid vertical surfaces, like walls, at your full Speed. You must start your movement on a horizontal surface. If you end a Stride off the ground, you must Stride along the surface again until you reach a horizontal surface or you begin to fall (though you can [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95), if applicable). If you have means of walking on water, such as with [_water walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=371) or similar abilities, you can also run along flimsy vertical surfaces, as well as vertical liquids such as a waterfall.

</column>

These brown leather shoes have surprisingly thick soles, as though a cobbler had recently repaired them. The tan laces always pull to exactly the right tautness for your feet and ankles to feel supported. You can perform the [Hustle](/Actions.aspx?ID=2626) exploration mode activity for twice as many minutes as normal, equal to your Constitution modifier × 20 (minimum 20).

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 12"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Boots of the Blight](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3693)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 78

**Price** 1,800 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Tanglebriar is not the only realm plagued by fiendish fungi. The soldiers of Nirmathas have long fought against a similar blight deep in Fangwood, and these boots are one of the more potent tools they’ve developed to help in this pursuit. Now that the Fangwood blight has been mostly contained, many of these boots have been gifted to elven soldiers, for they are equally useful to those who operate within Tanglebriar’s borders. They are also regarded as great trophies for the [demons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387) and cultists who dwell within Tanglebriar, for not only can they make use of these boots’ powers, but wearing something created by your enemy gives [Treerazer’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=324) agents yet another way to engage in psychological warfare—they often adorn their boots with severed elf ears, or worse! 

These leather boots remain covered in mud no matter how often they are cleaned. The oiled leather resists water and keeps the feet and legs dry even when wading through water, but the boots retain a damp, fungal smell reminiscent of rotting vegetation. While wearing the boots, you gain a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) and to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369).

**Activate—Swift Sidestep** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You are about to make a Reflex saving throw against an [environmental hazard](/Rules.aspx?ID=2588) or [terrain feature](/Rules.aspx?ID=1791);  **Effect** The boots help you to avoid the hazard or effect, granting you a +2 status bonus to your saving throw. If you succeed at the saving throw, you become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 minute, but can use the additional action only to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305).

**Activate—Fungal Stride** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You ignore the effects of [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 10 to damage caused by hazardous terrain. This activation lasts for 10 minutes.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Boots of the Dead](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3959)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 149

**Price** 35 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Perhaps you had no other choice than to steal the boots off a fallen soldier. Yours may have been worn out, full of holes, or even coming apart. Did you take them from a fallen ally or adversary? Everyone looks the same after war has its way. Nevertheless, the guilt you feel weighs you down. You gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws and DCs against forced movement.

**Activate—One of You** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You shuffle your boots, which still stink of the dead, causing one [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creature of your choice to think that you too are undead. The target is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against the next melee attack you attempt against it before the end of your current turn.

You pride yourself on being well prepared with weaponry for any situation. Your dark-gray boots might appear mundane, but you know that they can conjure a blade at any moment. Even the most thorough of searches can’t find a knife that doesn’t exist yet.

**Activate—Draw Secret Blade** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You reach down to your boot, draw a [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=358) from it, and make a ranged or melee Strike with it. This dagger is created magically and does not exist before being drawn. The dagger remains a physical object until the next time you use Draw Secret Blade, and it disappears as a new blade is created.

</title>

<traits>

---

The city of Riddleport is notorious for its noxious air and water. While some inhabitants tolerate the haze, most wear bootstrap respirators to filter out as many of the pollutants as possible. Designed by dwarf smiths operating the Gas Forges, the flexible face mask of a bootstrap respirator fits snugly over your mouth and nose, fastened by two adjustable leather straps. A manual pump inserted into your footwear or under the arm circulates air through tubes and over filters fitted into the front of the mask. While wearing a bootstrap respirator, you gain a +1 item bonus to any saves that require you to smell or taste, such as [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) and airborne [diseases](/Traits.aspx?ID=46).

This ornate copper band has a small ruby set in the center, flanked by a pair of dwarven runes. The wearer of this ring gains the ability to understand, read, and speak one common language of their choice, selected each morning as part of their daily preparations. In addition, the wearer receives a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to Make an Impression.

    right="Item 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bottle of Infinite Dust](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3929)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 143

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This plain, faintly green bottle full of sand looks deceptively mundane, though it contains a near endless supply of sand. A very slow but steady stream of sand can be poured from the bottle. Up to 1 pound of sand can be produced a day this way.

**Activate—Grit Geyser** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=585), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You aim the bottle and unleash a blast of sand. Scouring grit is released in a 15-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), dealing 4d4 slashing damage to all creatures in the area (DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).

**Activate—Sandstorm** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=585), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You dump out the bottle, creating a swirling sandstorm around you. A 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) is filled with blowing sand that obscures vision. This has the effects of mist. The air within the sandstorm is unbreathable; creatures in the area must [hold their breath](/Rules.aspx?ID=2439). Creatures entering or starting their turn in the sandstorm take 2d4 slashing damage (DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). Creatures with the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) trait or that are primarily made of liquid take double damage. This sandstorm lasts 10 minutes or until the bottle is corked with an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action, whichever comes first.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Tiny black motes swirl inside this crystalline vial. The vial can be thrown up to 20 feet, shattering and releasing the motes to absorb light within a 15-foot burst. Light sources within the motes' area of effect create a 5-foot radius of dim light instead of their normal light and light sources outside the motes to not illuminate the area within them. The darkness lasts for 1 minute, but will disperse immediately in a strong wind.

This bottle contains a shrunken bird preserved with its feathers intact. When opened, the contents reconstitute into a Gargantuan effigy of a great [roc](/Monsters.aspx?ID=352), which can appear in the air instead of on the ground. The roc [Grabs](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=18) up to two creatures, then [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) up to 90 feet and [Releases](/Actions.aspx?ID=83) the creatures. The creatures must be within 15 feet of the roc for it to Grab them; if any of them are unwilling to be [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20), the roc must [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) them with a +17 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) modifier or fail to pick them up.

**Craft Requirements** Supply the corpse of a roc.

The creatures must be within 15 feet of the roc for it to Grab them; if any of them are unwilling to be grabbed, the roc must Grapple them with a +17 Athletics modifier or fail to pick them up. Craft Requirements Supply the corpse of a roc.

This mirrored bottle contains various chemicals dissolved in two immiscible solvents. Shaking the bottle induces chemical reactions that cause it to glow. For 1 hour, the bottle sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) to the next 40 feet).

 During this hour, it can be thrown like a bomb. This requires a single action to Activate with a Strike, like other bombs, and deals the damage below. If it's not thrown within an hour of the first activation, it defuses harmlessly and is consumed.

The bomb deals 1d4 positive damage and 1 positive [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage, as well as 1d4 additional fire damage. As normal, positive damage harms only [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) and other creatures with [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42). Undead with a particular vulnerability to sunlight (such as [vampires](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=97) or [wraiths](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=164)) take the maximum amount of positive damage from bottled sunlight (4 instead of 1d4). For any ability that depends on the number of weapon dice bottled sunlight has, count only the positive damage dice.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Contract" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=329" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 164

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

With a handshake, you traded future wealth for a bottomless purse of gems and other valuables. Using the purse, you can always sell items for their normal sell value during downtime, even if you aren't anywhere near a settlement. You just put them into the purse, and within a day, the proper sale price appears in coins and gems. Once per day, from any distance, the entity that holds your bargained contract automatically sells a common [consumable](/Traits.aspx?ID=36) item in your possession, giving you back only half the normal amount for a sold item.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You deposit up to 30 gp of gems and coins in a separate pouch of the _bottomless purse_ while thinking of a common consumable item costing that amount of money. You then upend the pouch. The item you envisioned comes tumbling out into your hand.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

A magic item regarded as holy by followers of Cayden Cailean, this ornate metallic stein is always filled to the brim with delicious ale, no matter how much is drunk or spilled. If it is emptied (such as by being gulped quickly or upended onto the floor), the _bottomless stein_ will fill again within 1 round as long as it is right side up, though it’s impossible to transfer the ale to another container to sell it or store it for later. The exact type of ale with which the stein is filled is determined at the item’s creation, and cannot be changed thereafter.

The spikes of this _[+2](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [standard-grade adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2915) [morningstar](/Weapons.aspx?ID=363)_ have a faintly green shimmer, as if resembling Ayrzul’s crystalline teeth. The weapon vibrates briefly when first drawn in or carried into a radioactive area, with the intensity of the vibration correlating to the radioactivity’s strength. While you carry _Boughshatter_, you gain a +4 status bonus to saving throws against radiation, including [Ayrzul’s Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41). 

**Activate—Splintering Strike** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** Make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with the morningstar that deals an extra die of weapon damage. If you make this Strike against a [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=614), [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=668), or creature with the [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508) trait, the Strike ignores 10 points of the target’s resistances to bludgeoning and piercing damage, if any. By damaging such a creature, the morningstar causes the target’s flesh to explode in a shower of splinters that affect a 30-foot cone originating from the target’s space, dealing 8d6 piercing damage to creatures in the area (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). You and the target are unaffected by these splinters. 

**Activate—Absorb Corruption** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You take [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) or [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage;;  **Effect** You channel some of the toxic energy into _Boughshatter_, granting the weapon the effects of either a [_decaying weapon rune_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2835), grievous weapon rune, or wounding weapon rune for 1 minute. While under this effect, the morningstar glows with [dim green light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) in a 20-foot radius.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Bomb" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=21" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Splash" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=150" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 44

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Strike</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This bomb is made of volatile fluids that rapidly expand and harden when exposed to air. A boulder seed grants an item bonus to attack rolls and deals bludgeoning damage and bludgeoning splash damage, according to the bomb's type. When activated, the bomb fills a 5-foot cube with hardened foam, which has stats according to the bomb's type and which [pushes](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) a primary target of a certain size or smaller occupying that space 5 feet away from you. On a critical hit, the target also falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). The splash zone fills with rubble, creating difficult terrain. The “boulder” the bomb creates fails all saving throws and loses 1 Hardness per round, disintegrating into fine powder when the boulder's Hardness is reduced to 0. At that time, the difficult terrain the bomb created also disappears.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

No one is sure if Gorm brews this malty ale himself, but it seems to be an off-duty favorite of the Grand Archive faction leader. The brew packs a heavy punch, and while Gorm officially discourages drinking on the job, boulderhead bock does makes the drinker more self-assured and protects them from conditions that would addle their mental faculties. For 1 hour, you gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws against effects that would make you [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37). However, you also become less aware of your surroundings, taking a –2 item penalty to Perception for 1 hour.

---

_Bower fruit_ got its name from its association with [the Green Mother](/Deities.aspx?ID=93), a fey Eldest with a fondness for plants and manipulation, whose domain is known as the Hanging Bower. She uses these cursed fruits to keep mortals in her thrall, but it's unknown whether she created them or simply popularized their use.

 A _bower fruit_ condemns a non-fey who tastes it to never again be satisfied with the fare found in the mundane [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26). Any fruit can be cursed in this manner, but stone fruits such as peaches, plums, mangoes, and lychees are most common. Upon activating a bower fruit by eating it, you’re afflicted with the curse of decadence. You can’t recover from stage 1 of the curse naturally, even if you succeed at the save to do so.

You become [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) and take 1d4 damage each day that can’t be healed until you sate your hunger. No amount of eating food can sate your hunger during the spell’s duration, with one exception—food from the First World sates your hunger and suppresses the effects, but permanently increases the save DC by 1 (to a maximum of DC 35). After the week ends, if your hunger is still not sated, you take damage from [starvation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2603). (1 week); **Stage 2** As stage 1, plus you’re [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1; **Stage 3** As stage 1, plus you’re [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1 and sickened 1; **Stage 4** As stage 1, plus you’re drained 2, sickened 2, and [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 2.

---

_Bower fruit_ got its name from its association with [the Green Mother](/Deities.aspx?ID=453), a fey Eldest with a fondness for plants and manipulation, whose domain is known as the Hanging Bower. She uses these cursed fruits to keep mortals in her thrall, but it’s unknown whether she created them or simply popularized their use.

A _bower fruit_ condemns a non-[fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=599) who tastes it to never again be satisfied with [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=26) fare. Any fruit can be cursed in this manner, but stone fruits such as peaches, plums, mangoes, and lychees are most common. Upon activating a bower fruit by eating it, the fruit casts a 6th-level [_feast of ashes_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2351) on you (DC 30). This [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566) is permanent, but food from the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=35), rather than no food, can sate your accursed hunger. If you sate your hunger this way, you gain an [addiction](/Diseases.aspx?ID=15) as if First World food and drink were a drug for you (DC 30).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bracelet Of Buoyancy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5237)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 103

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This bracelet resembles a string of pearls filled with swirling air, making you more buoyant. While wearing the bracelet, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to Swim. 

**Activate—Float** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You’re submerged in water or another liquid; **Effect** You rapidly surface, rising 60 feet at the end of each of your turns. Once you reach the liquid’s surface, you can’t dive or sink for the next 10 minutes, and a creature that attempts to pull you beneath the surface must first succeed at a DC 17 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 17"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Bracers of Hammers](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2526)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds](/Sources.aspx?ID=203) pg. 69

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn bracers

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These brilliant golden bracers feature a hammer motif as part of their engravings. While wearing them, your body surges with strength and you gain a +3 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks and a +1 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) and [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40). If you succeed, but not critically succeed, at your check to Disarm a creature, the effects of your check last until the start of your next turn, instead until the start of the target's turn. If you succeed at a check to Trip a creature, it takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage or 4d6 bludgeoning damage on a critical success. When you invest the bracers, you either increase your Strength score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You reach for a foe and attempt to topple them with a powerful flip. Attempt an Athletics check to Trip a creature within reach. On a success, the creature is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) and takes 10d6 bludgeoning damage (double on a critical hit). If you knock the creature prone, it must also attempt a DC 35 Reflex save. On a failure, it drops any items it's holding.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Etchings of powerful bears decorate these brass bracers. <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 6"
    pfs=""
>
[Brain Cylinder](/Equipment.aspx?ID=953)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Malevolence</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Malevolence](/Sources.aspx?ID=88) pg. 66

**Price** 250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _brain cylinder_ allows the extracted brain of a Large or smaller creature to continue to function even after it has been removed from the body. As long as the brain remains in the cylinder, the creature remains alive and can continue to think, even though its body is dead. Detachable modules that fit into the base of the cylinder allow the brain to see, hear, or speak using a raspy speaker. So long as these are attached, the brain can speak and understand any languages it knew in life, though nothing within the cylinder compels it to do so if it is unwilling. It also retains its living alignment, and can use Intelligence-, Wisdom-, and Charisma-based skills. A standard _brain cylinder_ has one skill at +15, one at +13, and two at +11, as chosen by the GM.

 The brain retains no other abilities it possessed in life, including purely mental ones. [Mi-go](/Languages.aspx?ID=67) typically preserve humanoid brains in this manner when they wish to interrogate a creature at a later date, or when they wish to preserve a creature as a resource for consultation or research purposes, as a brain preserved in this manner can live for centuries. If a _brain cylinder_ is destroyed, the brain dies and its soul finally moves on to the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15). Restoring a brain in a _brain cylinder_ to its former body can be done by any effect that restores life (and, in most cases, any capable of creating a new body, since the original is typically missing or long gone).

 Note that the level 6 _brain cylinder_ presented above represents a level 6 creature's brain. A less powerful or more powerful brain can be placed in a _brain cylinder_, which can affect the brain cylinder's Perception, mental ability scores, Will save, and skill modifiers (and can drastically alter the value of the brain cylinder), but the physical properties of the _brain cylinder_ remain unchanged. Higher-level _brain cylinders_ can be crafted, with resistances and weaknesses increasing as appropriate to their level. However, they always have low AC and HP and terrible Fortitude and Reflex saves for a creature of the _brain cylinder's_ level (see the [Building Creatures](/Rules.aspx?ID=995) rules).

 You can open a _brain cylinder_ by taking three consecutive actions with the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) trait. If the _brain cylinder_ contains a brain, the brain dies 3 rounds after it's removed or if the cylinder is left open for more than 10 minutes. You can transfer a brain from one _brain cylinder_ to another with a DC 25 [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) (expert) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (expert) check. This is a two-action activity with the manipulate trait. On a critical failure, the brain dies.

</column>

_Bralani breath_ is a species of mint with small, green flowers, said to grow on battlefields where the opposing sides were equally matched. Sprigs of the flowers blow gently in a breeze of their own creation. If you cast [_mage armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1611) using _bralani breath_, you release a small blast of concussive air in an emanation of a size that depends on the catalyst’s type. </title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 73

**Price** 360 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in one hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This large tree branch is alive, despite having been harvested from the sugi tree it once belonged to. This long, flexible, and limber branch is a _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [whip](/Weapons.aspx?ID=404)_. When used to Strike, the branch snaps with the sound of a cracking whip but fills the air surrounding the point of impact with the pleasant scent of freshly cut cedar and a sprinkling of fallen leaves on the ground. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You place the _branch of the great sugi_ on the corpse of an evil creature, then cause the branch to suddenly grow into a sugi tree, up to 25 feet tall with a 2-foot-wide trunk. As it grows, it emits a pulse of soothing energy, restoring 3d8+8 Hit Points to all creatures in a 10-foot burst. A character can [Climb ](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374)the tree with a successful DC 10 Athletics check, and its branches effortlessly support the weight of any Medium or smaller creature. The sugi tree reverts to its whip form after 1 hour unless you transform it back before then. 

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You transform the _branch of the great sugi_ from its tree form back into its whip form.

A brass ear is a short, flared tube with one end narrow enough to comfortably fit against the ear canal. When using it to listen through a door, window, thin wall, or similar barrier, if the barrier would normally increase the DC of your Perception check to hear sounds on the other side, the DC increases by only half as much as normal. It's not suitable for improving your hearing in general, a role better served by a [hearing aids](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1347).

fields.text: Item 5+ Bravery Baldric Invested Magical Source Treasure Vault pg. 155 Usage worn Bulk L A bravery baldric is a belt that wraps around the shoulder and draws on your well of courage. When you critically succeed on a save against a fear effect or reduce your frightened condition to 0, the baldric gains 1 charge, which slightly alters the color. A bravery baldric can hold up to 2 charges, and its charges reset to 0 when you invest it. You can have only one bravery baldric invested at a time. Activate Two Actions command, envision; Requirements The baldric has a charge; Effect One charge in the baldric expires, and you gain its benefit, according to its type. Item 5 Bravery Baldric (Fleet) Source Treasure Vault pg. 146 Price 150 gp The baldric is grass green when charged, and it grants you the effects of fleet step . This baldric has the transmutation trait. Item 11 Bravery Baldric (Flight) Source Treasure Vault pg. 146 Price 1,250 gp The baldric is light blue when charged, and it grants you the effects of fly . This baldric has the transmutation trait. Item 9 Bravery Baldric (Haste) Source Treasure Vault pg. 146 Price 700 gp The baldric is silver when charged, and it grants you the effects of haste . This baldric has the transmutation trait. Item 7 Bravery Baldric (Restoration) Source Treasure Vault pg. 146 Price 350 gp The baldric is golden when charged, and it grants you the effects of a 2nd-level restoration . This baldric has the healing and necromancy traits. Item 11 Bravery Baldric (Restoration Greater) Source Treasure Vault pg. 146 Price 1,300 gp As the restoration baldric, but it grants 4th-level restoration . Item 11 Bravery Baldric (Stoneskin) Source Treasure Vault pg. 146 Price 1,400 gp The baldric is dark gray when charged, and it grants you the effects of stoneskin . This baldric has the abjuration trait.

<traits>

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 145

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

A _bravery baldric_ is a belt that wraps around the shoulder and draws on your well of courage. When you critically succeed on a save against a [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68) effect or reduce your [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) condition to 0, the baldric gains 1 charge, which slightly alters the color. A _bravery baldric_ can hold up to 2 charges, and its charges reset to 0 when you invest it. You can have only one _bravery baldric_ invested at a time.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;  **Requirements** The baldric has a charge; **Effect** One charge in the baldric expires, and you gain its benefit, according to its type.

---

The _brazier of harmony_ is a circular, orb-shaped censer etched with celebrating creatures shaking hands and dancing. The brazier contains a pleasant-smelling potpourri of dried flowers and incenses, designed to create a calm atmosphere that encourages meditation, thoughtfulness, and camaraderie. While holding the lit censer, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks, whether the censer is activated or not.

**Activate—Light Incense** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))**Cost** incense worth at least 1 sp; **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** When the incense is lit, pleasant, floral smoke surrounds the censer in a 20-foot emanation, creating a space of peace and harmony. Each creature that breathes the smoke is affected by 3rd-rank [_calm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=31) and is then temporarily immune for 24 hours. The spell's effects end when the incense burns out.

---

Constructed of dull gray metal, this [breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=10) is decorated with the symbol of a craggy black mountaintop. This breastplate functions as a _+3 [greater resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) breastplate_. When you're [Shoved](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) or otherwise [forced to move](/Rules.aspx?ID=451), you can reduce the amount you move by up to 10 feet. When you invest the breastplate, you either increase your Constitution modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You pound a solid and constant rhythm on your breastplate and cast a 7th-level [_regeneration_](/Spells.aspx?ID=248) spell on yourself.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** With a single tap, you gain immunity to [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) for 1 minute.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You fail or critically fail a Fortitude saving throw;  **Effect** If you failed the saving throw, it becomes a success. If you critically failed, it becomes a failure instead.

</column>

This breastplate functions as a +3 greater resilient breastplate . When you’re Shoved or otherwise forced to move, you can reduce the amount you move by up to 10 feet. When you invest the breastplate, you either increase your Constitution score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever is higher. Activate Two Actions Interact; Frequency once per day; Effect You pound a solid and constant rhythm on your breastplate and cast a 7th-level regeneration spell on yourself. Activate Single Action Interact; Frequency once per day; Effect With a single tap, you gain immunity to poison for 1 minute. Activate Reaction envision; Frequency once per day; Trigger You fail or critically fail a Fortitude saving throw; Effect If you failed the saving throw, it becomes a success. If you critically failed, it becomes a failure instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 8+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Breath Blaster](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1165)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 154

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _breath blaster_ is a _[+1 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [blunderbuss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=196)_ most commonly crafted from the trachea of a dragon, though other creatures with breath attacks or the ability to spit energy are occasionally used. The implementation of the dragon’s trachea allows the firearm to unleash a torrent of pure energy in the form of gouts of flame or bolts of electricity. A _breath blaster’s_ Strikes deal either [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) damage, depending on the dragon type or other creature from which it was made, though it can otherwise be used like a normal blunderbuss. A _breath blaster_ also can be activated to fire a [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) of energy in a 30-foot line or 15-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), chosen when it’s created and typically corresponding to the shape of the breath attack used by the type of dragon or creature from which the _breath blaster_ was created.

In theory, the foundational techniques required to create a _breath blaster_ would allow for other damage types, but such _breath blasters_ would require the trachea from the correct dragon or creature type and additional creation techniques, making such a _breath blaster_ rare rather than uncommon.

**Activate—Breath Blast** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You fire the _breath blaster_, dealing 4d6 damage of the appropriate type in the appropriate area. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save (or Fortitude save if the damage is poison).

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the trachea of a ritually hunted dragon or other creature with a breath weapon with the appropriate damage type and area (line or cone) for the _breath blaster_.

</column>

fields.text: Item 8+ Breath Blaster Uncommon Evocation Magical Source Guns & Gears pg. 154 Usage held in 2 hands Bulk 2 Base Weapon Blunderbuss A breath blaster is a +1 striking blunderbuss most commonly crafted from the trachea of a dragon, though other creatures with breath weapons or the ability to spit energy are occasionally used. The implementation of the dragon’s trachea allows the firearm to unleash a torrent of pure energy in the form of gouts of flame or bolts of electricity. A breath blaster’s Strikes deal either acid, cold, electricity, fire, or poison damage, depending on the dragon type or other creature from which it was made, though it can otherwise be used like a normal blunderbuss. A breath blaster also can be activated to fire a line of energy in a 30-foot line or 15-foot cone, chosen when it’s created and typically corresponding to the shape of the breath weapon used by the type of dragon or creature from which the breath blaster was created. In theory, the foundational techniques required to create a breath blaster would allow for other damage types, but such breath blasters would require the trachea from the correct dragon or creature type and additional creation techniques, making such a breath blaster rare rather than uncommon. Activate Two Actions Interact (evocation, magical) Frequency once per minute; Effect You fire the breath blaster , dealing 4d6 damage of the appropriate type in the appropriate area. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 24 basic Reflex save (or Fortitude save if the damage is poison). Craft Requirements The initial raw materials must include the trachea of a ritually hunted dragon or other creature with a breath weapon with the appropriate damage type and area (line or cone) for the breath blaster . Item 8 Breath Blaster Source Guns & Gears pg. 154 Price 500 gp Item 14 Breath Blaster (Greater) Source Guns & Gears pg. 154 Price 4,500 gp The greater breath blaster’s activation deals 6d6 damage and the DC is 31. It’s a +2 greater striking blunderbuss . Item 18 Breath Blaster (Major) Source Guns & Gears pg. 154 Price 24,000 gp The major breath blaster’s activation deals 10d6 damage, the DC is 38, and the area increases to either a 60-foot line or a 30-foot cone, chosen when it’s created. It’s a +3 greater striking blunderbuss .

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 8+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Breath Blaster](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1165)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 154

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _breath blaster_ is a _[+1 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [blunderbuss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=196)_ most commonly crafted from the trachea of a dragon, though other creatures with breath attacks or the ability to spit energy are occasionally used. The implementation of the dragon’s trachea allows the firearm to unleash a torrent of pure energy in the form of gouts of flame or bolts of electricity. A _breath blaster’s_ Strikes deal either [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) damage, depending on the dragon type or other creature from which it was made, though it can otherwise be used like a normal blunderbuss. A _breath blaster_ also can be activated to fire a [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) of energy in a 30-foot line or 15-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), chosen when it’s created and typically corresponding to the shape of the breath attack used by the type of dragon or creature from which the _breath blaster_ was created.

In theory, the foundational techniques required to create a _breath blaster_ would allow for other damage types, but such _breath blasters_ would require the trachea from the correct dragon or creature type and additional creation techniques, making such a _breath blaster_ rare rather than uncommon.

**Activate—Breath Blast** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You fire the _breath blaster_, dealing 4d6 damage of the appropriate type in the appropriate area. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save (or Fortitude save if the damage is poison).

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the trachea of a ritually hunted dragon or other creature with a breath weapon with the appropriate damage type and area (line or cone) for the _breath blaster_.

[Breath of the Mantis God](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3491)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Prey for Death</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Inhaled" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=634" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=669" />
<trait label="Virulent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=726" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 103

**Price** 200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

To prevent one of their victims from being brought back to life, Red Mantis assassins often poison targets with the breath of the mantis god. After a creature is poisoned by this concoction, internal hemorrhaging frequently results in blood issuing from the creature's mouth—a condition referred to by the assassins as having “the breath of the mantis god.” While a creature can attempt to recover normally from the persistent bleed damage caused by breath of the mantis god, the persistent bleed damage will return if the poison's duration is still ongoing. If a creature dies from the poison's effects, the toxin lingers tenaciously in the creature's flesh for 1 year. During this time, if an attempt is made to bring such a slain creature back to life that doesn't create a new body for the deceased (such as with a 7th-rank [_resurrect_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=123) ritual), the lingering effects of breath of the mantis god attempts to counteract the resurrection ([counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) modifier +17, counteract rank 5). A spell like [_extract poison_](/Spells.aspx?ID=907) can be used to decontaminate a corpse for easier resurrection, but simpler magic such as cleanse cuisine cannot. A 5th-rank or higher cleanse affliction can also attempt to counteract lingering breath of the mantis god.

 **Saving Throw** DC 29 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 minutes; **Stage 1** 3d6 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) and [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1 (1 minute); **Stage 2** 3d8 persistent bleed and drained 1 (1 minute); **Stage 3** 3d10 persistent bleed and drained 2 (1 minute)

</column>

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 183

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to firearm (firing mechanism)

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These spring-loaded inserts can be fitted into the breech of a [double-barreled](/Traits.aspx?ID=403) firearm over the course of 10 minutes or during the firearm's daily maintenance. After the weapon is fired, the ejectors hasten the reloading process by ejecting the spent detritus from the fired rounds. This allows you to reload both barrels of the double-barreled weapon as a single Interact action the next time you reload the weapon as long as you do so before the end of your next turn. However, the ejectors are consumed in the process, and you must spend the time to insert a new set to gain the benefit again.

fields.text: Item 3 Breech Ejectors Uncommon Consumable Source Guns & Gears pg. 183 PFS Note Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons. Price 10 gp Usage attached to firearm (firing mechanism) These spring-loaded inserts can be fitted into the breech of a double-barreled firearm over the course of 10 minutes or during the firearm’s daily maintenance. After the weapon is fired, the ejectors hasten the reloading process by ejecting the spent detritus from the fired rounds. This allows you to reload both barrels of the double-barreled weapon as a single Interact action the next time you reload the weapon as long as you do so before the end of your next turn. However, the ejectors are consumed in the process, and you must spend the time to insert a new set to gain the benefit again.

When a brewer makes a batch of something they'd rather not drink, they often boil it down; add myrrh, mugwort extract, and violet salt; and sell it to chefs looking for cheap sandwich fillings. The thick, salty sourness ruins the taste of most other food, but it also creates a strong desire to live to taste anything else. For 1 hour after consumption, you gain a +2 item bonus to saves against [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) and [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) effects. In addition, your [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9) value decreases by 1 (minimum 0). You can reduce the doomed condition with brewer's regret only once per day, and after you do, you can't reduce the doomed condition from the [_restoration_](/Spells.aspx?ID=258) spell that same day (or vice versa).

May contain spoilers from Kingmaker **Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 584 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 **Base Weapon** [Bastard Sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=15) --- _Briar_ was formed ages ago by [the Eldest](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=7) when they tore from Nyrissa's mind and spirit her capability to love, then solidified this emotional energy into a sword. They entrusted _Briar's_ safe keeping to [the Lantern King](/Deities.aspx?ID=95), who mischievously kept moving the sword from world to world, always near to the regions Nyrissa was focused on but always hidden from her so that he could privately enjoy the delicious irony that the thing she sought so ardently was always kept just out of reach. When first recovered by the PCs, _Briar_ is a _+3 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=15)_, but its additional powers remain dormant. These powers can be awakened as the PCs progress through Chapter 10. The process of awakening _Briar_ requires that the weapon be present when [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=10) blooms are defeated or when powerful creatures from the First World are slain—_Briar_ need not be the weapon that defeats a bloom or slays a monster, but it must be in the immediate area (within 500 feet). Defeating a bloom or slaying a 17th-level or greater monster from the First World— including all creatures closely associated with a bloom—gives _Briar_ a Sharpness Point. As it accumulates these points, it gains additional powers, as detailed below. Once _Briar_ gains the capability to speak, it can relate to its partner the sad tale of its creation, including the fact that it was created by the Lantern King using Nyrissa's capacity to love. _Briar_ knows that without love, Nyrissa is as good as dead, and it suspects that only by being used to slay Nyrissa can it be returned to her soul. It doesn't know about the Lantern King's additional machinations, the nature of the _Apology_, or Nyrissa's reasons for attacking the Stolen Lands, and as such doesn't realize there is another method to be reunited with the nymph queen—see the end of Chapter 10. The first time _Briar_ is brought within 30 feet of Nyrissa, it automatically gains enough Sharpness Points to reach 20 points. --- **1 Sharpness Point** _Briar_ becomes a _+3 greater striking [shifting](/Equipment.aspx?ID=302) cold iron bastard sword_. ---
**4 Sharpness Points** _Briar_ becomes a _+3 major striking shifting cold iron bastard sword_. It gains the [Intelligent](/Traits.aspx?ID=280) trait, becomes chaotic neutral, and gains the following statistics.
**Perception** +30, normal vision and hearing within 30 feet
**Communication** empathy (partner only)
**Skills** [First World Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +30, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +28
**Int** +0, **Wis** +0, **Cha** +3
**Will** +30 **Activate** command; **Frequency** three times per day; **Effect** _Briar_ casts [_barkskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=20) on its partner. --- **8 Sharpness Points** _Briar_ becomes a _+4 major striking shifting cold iron bastard sword_. Its statistics improve as follows.
**Perception** +32, normal vision, [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), and hearing within 60 feet
**Communication** speech ([Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), and [Sylvan](/Languages.aspx?ID=10))
**Skills** First World Lore +32, Nature +30
**Int** +2, **Wis** +2, **Cha** +5 **Will** +32 **Activate** command; **Frequency** three times per day; **Effect** _Briar_ casts a 4th-level [_barkskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=20) on its partner. **Activate** ; **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** _Briar_ damages a plant creature; **Effect** _Briar_ draws moisture out of the plant creature's body, dealing 10d10 negative damage (DC 39 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save) --- **14 Sharpness Points** _Briar_ becomes a _+4 major striking shifting cold iron bastard sword_. Against denizens of the First World, it also functions as a [_vorpal_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=308) weapon. Its statistics improve as follows.
**Perception** +34, normal vision, darkvision, and hearing within 120 feet
**Communication** speech and [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) (Aklo, Common, and Sylvan)
**Skills** First World Lore +34, Nature +32
**Int** +4, **Wis** +4, **Cha** +7
**Will** +34 **Activate** command; **Frequency** three times per day; **Effect** _Briar_ casts a 6th-level barkskin on its partner. **Activate** ; **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** _Briar_ damages a plant creature; **Effect** _Briar_ draws moisture out of the plant creature's body, dealing 12d10 negative damage (DC 41 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save) **Activate** ; **Frequency** once per month; **Trigger** _Briar's_ partner would die; **Effect** _Briar_ casts [_breath of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=29) on its partner. --- **20 Sharpness Points** _Briar_ becomes a _+4 major striking shifting cold iron vorpal bastard sword_. Its statistics improve as follows.
**Perception** +36, normal vision, darkvision, and hearing within 60 feet
**Communication** speech and telepathy (Aklo, Common, and Sylvan)
**Skills** First World Lore +36, Nature +34
**Int** +6, **Wis** +6, **Cha** +9
**Will** +36 **Activate** command; **Frequency** three times per day; **Effect** _Briar_ casts an 8th-level [_barkskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=20) on its partner. **Activate** ; **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** _Briar_ damages a plant creature; **Effect** _Briar_ draws moisture out of the plant creature's body, dealing 14d10 negative damage (DC 43 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save) **Activate** ; **Frequency** once per month; **Trigger** _Briar's_ partner would die; **Effect** _Briar_ resurrects its partner. The partner returns to life with full Hit Points and the same spells prepared and points in their pools they had when they died, but still suffering from any long-term debilitations of the old body. The target is also permanently changed in some way that shifts their appearance slightly toward that of Nyrissa's, such as a green streak in the hair, a few thorny growths on the body, or a slight greenish cast to their skin. **Activate** ; **Trigger** _Briar's_ partner Strikes Nyrissa with _Briar_ for the first time in a round; **Effect** Nyrissa must make a successful DC 50 Fortitude save to resist being [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) (stunned 3 on a critical failure). _Briar's_ partner gains a +4 item bonus to all saving throws against Nyrissa's spells for 1 minute. **Destruction** The Lantern King can will _Briar's_ destruction if he chooses. Alternately, defeating the Lantern King's aspect (see page 600) causes the sword's destruction. Once _Briar_ is destroyed, Nyrissa regains the capability to love once again, but what she does next will depend on how the PCs treated her—assuming she survives. If Nyrissa is slain, _Briar_ immediately loses 1d6 Sharpness points. It can never again gain Sharpness points, and it continues to lose more at the rate of 1d6 every 24 hours. Once _Briar's_ Sharpness points drop to 0 in this way, the sword is destroyed.

Alternately, defeating the Lantern King's aspect (see page 600) causes the sword's destruction. Once Briar is destroyed, Nyrissa regains the capability to love once again, but what she does next will depend on how the PCs treated her—assuming she survives. If Nyrissa is slain, Briar immediately loses 1d6 Sharpness points. It can never again gain Sharpness points, and it continues to lose more at the rate of 1d6 every 24 hours. Once Briar's Sharpness points drop to 0 in this way, the sword is destroyed.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

This rune causes a weapon to transform into pure, brilliant energy. The weapon deals an additional 1d4 fire damage on a successful Strike, as well as 1d4 good damage to [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=70) and 1d4 positive damage to [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). On a critical hit, the target must succeed at a DC 29 Fortitude save or be [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 round.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100))    **Effect** You plunge your weapon into darkness to return the light. Attempt a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check with a counteract level of 5 and a +19 counteract modifier to end a magical [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) effect whose area is within reach of the weapon.
