**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 200 _[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) When using a broadleaf shield, the season is the current season where the player is located._ **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- Though it resembles an enormous leaf freshly plucked from a tree, a _broadleaf shield_ is extremely durable. It also regrows rapidly, fully repairing itself when broken if it's left in sunlight for 10 consecutive minutes. At each dawn, the leaf transforms to an appearance appropriate for the season. While you're wielding the shield, you gain resistance to a damage type depending on the shield's color. This resistance doubles while you have the shield raised.
  • **Pink** (void resistance) In spring, the leaf is a delicate blossom-like pink and exudes the energy of life.
  • **Green** (fire resistance) In summer, the leaf is a deep, rich green with a waxy coating.
  • **Orange** (poison resistance) In autumn, the leaf turns orange, red, or yellow and dehydrates slightly.
  • **Brown** (cold resistance) In winter, the leaf turns dead, dry, and brown.
**Activate—Change Season** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The shield transforms as though living through seasons in a moment, becoming the color of your choice for 5 minutes. Broadleaf Shield **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 200 **Price** 225 gp **Bulk** L --- The shield has Hardness 4, HP 16, and BT 8. The resistances are 3 (6 when raised). Broadleaf Shield (Greater) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 200 **Price** 675 gp **Bulk** L --- The shield has Hardness 6, HP 24, and BT 12. The resistances are 4 (8 when raised). Broadleaf Shield (Major) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 200 **Price** 2,750 gp **Bulk** L --- The shield has Hardness 8, HP 32, and BT 16. The resistances are 5 (10 when raised). Broadleaf Shield (True) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 200 **Price** 13,750 gp **Bulk** L --- The shield has Hardness 10, HP 40, and BT 20. The resistances are 6 (12 when raised).

[Broken Ram's Thorn](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3256)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Catalyst" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=791" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 118

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row>[Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) (add 1 action)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The thorny growths on a [rosethorn ram's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1274) horns break off into jagged pieces when these animals fight. When used to enhance the two-action version of a [_howling blizzard_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1559) spell, these thorns cause the squares directly adjacent to every creature within the spell's area of effect to become littered with icy caltrops. The first creature that moves into each affected square must succeed at an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) check with a DC equal to spell's save DC or take an amount of cold damage equal to the spell's rank. When a creature takes damage from the icy caltrops, enough are damaged that other creatures moving into that square are safe.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3+"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Broken Tusk Pendant](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1508)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 77

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The followers of the Broken Tusk have passed down their custom of crafting and gifting these small ivory necklaces for generations. They're typically made from mammoth tusk (though any type of ivory will do), and each is carved to resemble a particular kind of animal—usually a raven, a moose, an ox, or an otter. Because tradition dictates that Broken Tusk followers take ivory only from already-dead animals, _Broken Tusk pendants_ are especially rare; if an individual loses their pendant, it might be years before they acquire the materials necessary to fashion a replacement. _Broken Tusk pendants_ bear no magical powers if they are made for oneself; only gifted pendants have true magical properties.

 You wear a _Broken Tusk pendant_ like jewelry or tie it to your clothing. A _Broken Tusk pendant_ grants you a +1 item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks; this bonus increases to +2 when you [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=58) of the specific kind depicted by the pendant.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** An [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) targets you with a melee attack, and you can see the animal;  **Effect** You gain a +1 item bonus to AC against the triggering attack, or a +2 item bonus if the animal is the specific kind depicted by the pendant.

</column>

You can choose whether to use this once-per-day effect after the animal misses you.

<traits>

---

This piece of silver or gold jewelry is adorned with miniature images of kite shields and can be used to fasten a cloak or cape. The brooch automatically absorbs [_magic missile_](/Spells.aspx?ID=180) spells targeting you. A _brooch of shielding_ can absorb 30 individual _magic missiles_ before it melts and becomes useless. Sometimes when found, a _brooch of shielding_ has already absorbed a number of missiles.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Broom of Flying](/Equipment.aspx?ID=251)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 572

**Price** 1,900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This broom has a tenuous connection to gravity, and it tends to drift even while stowed. You can ride on the broom using one hand to guide it, and the broom can carry up to one passenger in addition to you. The broom moves at a fly Speed of 20 feet. The broom can carry only so much, taking a –10-foot penalty to its Speed if laden with more than 20 Bulk, and crashing to the ground if it carries more than 30 Bulk.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** You name a destination on the same plane, and the broom speeds toward it at a fly Speed of 40 feet. You must either clutch the broom with two hands in order to ride it, or you need to release the broom to send it off with no rider. If you don’t have a good idea of the location, layout, and general direction of the destination, or if your named destination is on another plane, the broom wanders aimlessly, circling back to its starting location after 30 minutes.

If the broom carries a rider, this activation lasts until 4 hours pass (typically 16 miles of travel), the broom reaches its destination, or you Dismiss the activation. If the broom doesn’t have a rider, the activation lasts until the broom reaches its destination. When the activation ends, the broom floats to the ground and can’t be activated again for 1 hour.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Bubbling Scale](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1497)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Threshold of Knowledge</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Threshold of Knowledge](/Sources.aspx?ID=109) pg. 10

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This dark, iridescent scale is about the size of a small coin. When you swallow the scale, you immediately grow a patch of scales that cover the majority of your body. For 1 hour, you can hold your breath for 15 rounds plus your Constitution modifier (instead of 5 rounds + your Constitution modifier) before [drowning](/Rules.aspx?ID=468). It has no effect in non-aquatic environments that require you to hold your breath. After this time, the scales wither and fall off your body.

**Bulk** 1
</row>

</row>

---

A _bullhook_ is a stout rod about 4 feet long with a blunt hook on the end. Too dull to be useful as a weapon, a _bullhook_ is instead used to direct animals in training or in performing their tasks. A _bullhook_ grants you an item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=58) while you are holding it.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You wave the _bullhook_ to produce the effects of a [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=45) spell. This spell loses the [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101) trait and can target only animals.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _command_ of the appropriate level.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

---

A _bullhook_ is a stout rod about 4 feet long with a blunt hook on the end. Too dull to be useful as a weapon, a _bullhook_ is instead used to direct animals in training or in performing their tasks. A _bullhook_ grants you an item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=58) while you are holding it.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You wave the _bullhook_ to produce the effects of a [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=45) spell. This spell loses the [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101) trait and can target only animals.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _command_ of the appropriate level.

    level="1"
    right="Item 0"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Buoyancy Vest](/Equipment.aspx?ID=863)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 114

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This canvas vest has been filled with cork shavings, tightly folded, and sewn shut. Wearing a buoyancy vest allows you to float in water with a lowered risk of sinking. If you end your turn in water while wearing a buoyancy vest and haven't succeeded at a [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) action that turn, attempt a DC 5 flat check. On a success, you do not sink, though you can still get moved by the current, as determined by the GM. The GM can also determine whether the vest is more or less effective in different weather conditions, raising the DC in rough waters or lowering the DC in calm water.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 120

**Price** 250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _[+1 ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41)_ has several large pouches along the sides of the torso as well as the front and back sides of the legs. While wearing this armor, you can quickly inflate these large pouches with air, allowing you to float in water.

**Activate—Flotation** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You inflate large pouches that allow you to float. You gain a [swim Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2351) equal to half your land Speed. You can swim only along the surface of the water while this is active. You can stow the flotation devices as a 1-minute exploration activity. If the pouches take any damage (AC 10, Hardness 0), they quickly deflate, ending the effect.

</column>

[Burglar's Rosebud](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3733)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=60" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay](/Sources.aspx?ID=243) pg. 76

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Though originally intended to protect a [green man](/Deities.aspx?ID=221)’s favorite agents against predation by pesky herbivores, thieves have adapted the design to help them disperse guard animals. The soft flower bud belies the horrible perfume contained within. Activated by cracking open the petals, the rosebud exudes a noxious cloud that has the [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664) trait for 10 minutes. If dropped, it fills a 10-foot-[burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385). If you carry it in one hand and periodically waft it as a free action, the rosebud instead gives you a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). Creatures that enter or start their turn in the cloud must succeed at a Fortitude save against the listed DC or become [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1. [Animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=531) and [beasts](/Traits.aspx?ID=547) that critically fail are also [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) for 1 round. A creature that successfully saves against the burglar’s rosebud becomes temporarily immune to the effects for 24 hours.

>
[Burnished Plating](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1427)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Adjustment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=380" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 104

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** applied to metal armor

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These highly polished metal plates can be added to any armor. While wearing armor with burnished plating, you gain the Sunshine! reaction. However, you take a –4 circumstance penalty to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks except in darkness, and your armor's Strength entry increases its value by 2, requiring you to have a higher Strength score to overcome the armor's penalties. Even if you meet your armor's new Strength entry, you still take the penalty to Stealth checks. When you are critically hit by an attack that deals bludgeoning damage, burnished plating stops working until someone spends 10 minutes repairing and polishing it; this doesn't require a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) check.

 **Sunshine!** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature you can see targets you with an attack; **Requirements** You are in an area of bright light; **Effect** You twist to reflect light in your foe's eyes. The attacking creature must succeed at a DC 3 flat check or the attack fails. The attacker doesn't need to roll this flat check if it has a precise sense other than vision or if it would already need to roll a flat check with a higher DC to target you, such as if you are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 15"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Busine of Divine Reinforcement](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1566)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Good" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=83" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 89

**Price** 6,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

**Access** Knights of Lastwall have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This long, straight, trumpet-like instrument is made of well-polished brass and adorned with imagery of angels fighting demons or religious symbols. When played as an instrument, the busine generates powerful and harmonious notes and grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You play a few notes on the busine. Evil creatures within 60 feet who hear the notes must succeed at a DC 34 Will save or be [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) for 1 round, or 2 rounds on a critical failure; this is an [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93) effect.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> command, envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You blow into the busine and conjure a [celestial](/Languages.aspx?ID=16) with the effects of a 6th-level [_summon celestial_](/Spells.aspx?ID=317) spell, but there are no alignment restrictions to define which celestials you can call. The celestial will fight only evil creatures and leaves after all present evil creatures have been defeated or the spell's duration ends, whichever comes first. You can Sustain the Activation to extend the spell's duration, as normal. If you have a deity and the conjured celestial's alignment is one of your deity's preferred alignments, the effect functions as a normal 6th-level _summon celestial_ spell instead, meaning the celestial will fight any creature, not just evil creatures, and will perform other tasks as you command.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Base Weapon** [Battle Axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=16)

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

With an aerodynamic cutting edge and a curved handle, this _+2 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [battle axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=16)_ is perfectly suited to whirling motions, and in fact seems like it wants to whirl free from your grip. A Strike with this axe that benefits from the [sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=194) trait's circumstance bonus on attack rolls also gains a +2 circumstance bonus to the damage roll.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You hurl the axe, which spins at great speed as it flies to a distant point and returns to you, leaving a trail of carnage. Each creature in a 120-foot line must succeed at a DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save or take damage equal to the weapon's melee damage, including your Strength modifier.

Hewn from a solid block of ensorcelled stone, this _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=379)_ is monumental in heft as well as destructive force. The weapon is named for the disbelieving leaders of the Seventh Army of Exploration, who denied the power of such a weapon and claimed their losses came from natural disasters. When wielded against creatures that are larger than you, the sword gains the [sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=708) trait. 

**Activate—Shatter Legions** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=585)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You smash the sword down upon the ground with the anger of a conquered land and a subjugated people. Each creature in a 30-foot cone takes 4d12 piercing damage with a DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save as the earth shatters beneath their feet. Until the beginning of your next turn, you gain the benefits of [standard cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) from the broken soil around you.

[Calamity Glass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1641)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Scrying" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=141" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 160

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This mirror appears to give warnings about the future, but subtle and malevolent hands designed the silver-framed glass to lure heroes into bringing doom upon those they hope to save.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You activate the _calamity glass_ and obtain a vision related to a likely action or event within the next 48 hours. The _calamity glass_ decides what vision to show, though if you think about a specific event, the vision is typically at least tangentially related.

 No matter what, the mirror shows only tragedies. The mirror's visions are accurate but misleading, as they depict tragedies that could be averted but in so doing might lead to greater suffering.

 For example, a _calamity glass_ might show a family starving as the result of harbor officials turning away a boatload of improperly documented grain. Without intervention, this future will come to pass. What the mirror didn't show is the grain was improperly labeled and carelessly stored, resulting in its contamination with poisonous mold capable of killing hundreds. Purifying and then distributing the grain would avert both the _calamity glass'_s vision and the greater suffering its curse attempted to create.

[Calamity's Bane Tattoo](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5174)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 241

**Price** 250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This small tattoo of a stylized lidded or clouded eye radiating lines of power is inked on a part of your body that you cannot easily see with your own eyes, such as the nape of your neck, behind your ears, or your interscapular region. This tattoo protects you during calamity as well as uncertainty, guiding your intuition to take subconscious actions and precautions to shelter you in a thousand unknown ways. When you are affected by a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect or a [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566), your shrouded eye tattoo emits an intense sensation akin to pins and needles, alerting you that something is awry, though the specific nature of the danger might be unknown to you. 

**Activate—Alleviate Uncertainty** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Trigger** You make a check for an action that has the secret trait or that has been affected by a misfortune effect;  **Effect** You gain a +1 status bonus to the check associated with the triggering action.

</column>

A _called_ weapon can be teleported to its owner's hand.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (command, envision);     **Effect** You imprint upon the weapon, proclaiming yourself as its owner. This allows you to use the rune's second activation until someone else uses this activation or succeeds at a Will save to prevent you from using the second activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;     **Effect** You extend your hand and call the weapon. If the weapon is in another creature's possession, that creature can attempt a Will save against your Will DC. If the creature succeeds, your bond as the owner is broken, and you can't use this activation again until you use the first activation to restore the connection.

<traits>

**Price** 3 sp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 1

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

These four-pronged metal spikes can damage a creature's feet. You can scatter caltrops in an empty square adjacent to you with an Interact action. The first creature that moves into that square must succeed at a DC 14 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) check or take 1d4 piercing damage and 1 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). A creature taking persistent bleed damage from caltrops takes a –5-foot penalty to its Speed. Spending an Interact action to pluck the caltrops free reduces the DC to stop the bleeding. Once a creature takes damage from caltrops, enough are ruined that other creatures moving into the square are safe. Deployed caltrops can be salvaged and reused if no creatures took damage from them. Otherwise, enough are ruined that they can't be salvaged.

---

Camouflage dye uses a variety of alchemically treated paints and crushed crystals to make the user particularly hard to distinguish from their surroundings. When you Activate the dye by sprinkling it on yourself or a creature within reach, the target and its clothing change colors, blending into their surroundings until the target makes a sudden movement. The target can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) without [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) or [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) for 10 minutes. If the target uses a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) or moves at more than half its Speed, after that action is completed, the effects of camouflage powder end and the creature ceases to be [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39).

Camouflage dye uses a variety of alchemically treated paints and crushed crystals to make the user particularly hard to distinguish from their surroundings. When you Activate the dye by sprinkling it on yourself or a creature within reach, the target and its clothing change colors, blending into their surroundings until the target makes a sudden movement. The target can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) without [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) or [concealment](/Rules.aspx?ID=424) for 10 minutes.     right="Item 3+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Camouflage Suit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1201)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 178

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This lightweight mesh fits easily over light armor. The suit is designed to incorporate local flora and ground clutter into the mesh to help you blend in seamlessly with the environment. Due to the abrasive nature of the materials used, this item is unsuitable for use by unarmored characters. You can prepare the suit for use within your current environment by using an exploration activity that takes at least 10 minutes, but sometimes longer if the materials are hard to find or the environment is unusual enough to warrant additional difficulty in preparing camouflage that can blend with it consistently.

 A suit prepared in this manner grants you a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks while you attempt to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) in the specific environment it has been prepared for. The suit remains usable in this manner until you rest for the night, though it doesn't grant the benefit whenever you aren't in the appropriate environment. The GM might rule that some environments are unusual enough that you can't create a camouflage suit appropriate for the environment.

Due to the abrasive nature of the materials used, this item is unsuitable for use by unarmored characters. You can prepare the suit for use within your current environment by using an exploration activity that takes at least 10 minutes, but sometimes longer if the materials are hard to find or the environment is unusual enough to warrant additional difficulty in preparing camouflage that can blend with it consistently.

[Camouflaging Chromatophores](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3180)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Graft" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=790" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 97

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** implanted

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Special cells in your skin can change color to help you blend in with your environment. You gain the listed item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks to [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) and [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404).

**Activate—Background Adaptation** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** For 1 minute, you can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) without needing [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) or [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) to do so. This doesn’t allow you to [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) without ending your movement in cover or concealment, however, as your skin’s attempts to match the background as you move produce noticeable rippling waves of color.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<traits>

**Price** 95 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

pfs="Standard"

<traits>

</traits>

**Price** 665 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The bonus is +2, and you can use Background Adaptation once per hour.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

---

Knights make use of this magically treated powder to help hide their camps while traveling through the Gravelands or other dangerous regions. When you toss the powder into a campfire or other sizable fire, the fire produces a thin mist that enshrouds everything in a 10-foot emanation from the fire. The mist creates protective illusions that remain for up to 12 hours and make it difficult to spot the area from afar. You can end the effect earlier by putting out the fire. Light and smoke produced in the area aren't visible from outside the area. The illusions don't prevent sound from traveling nor prevent the area or its inhabitants from being seen.

 A creature outside the area that uses the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) action or [Search](/Actions.aspx?ID=519) activity to examine the area or look for smoke and light coming from that direction can attempt a DC 18 Perception check to disbelieve the illusion.

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 89 **Price** 500 gp **Bulk** L when not activated **Access** Knights of Lastwall have access to this item. --- Used to facilitate the care of mounts during long campaigns or when it's necessary to move camp frequently, this object appears to be a simple, worn wooden horseshoe. **Activate** 1 minute (command, Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You place the horseshoe on the ground and it unfolds into a spacious stable with a wide central aisle, stalls to accommodate up to eight horses, and sufficient feed and water to sustain the horses for 1 day. The stalls can house other quadrupedal mounts, but the stable provides only horse feed, which might be unsuitable for other creatures. As a 1-minute activity, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, you can alter the shape of the stalls to accommodate different mounts, though the space available within the stable never changes, only the layout.
A metal horseshoe hangs inside the stable near the entrance. You can remove the horseshoe with an Interact action, which causes the stable to fold into the horseshoe, leaving it again looking as if it's made of worn wood.

Used to facilitate the care of mounts during long campaigns or when it's necessary to move camp frequently, this object appears to be a simple, worn wooden horseshoe. Activate 1 minute (command, Interact; Frequency once per day; Effect You place the horseshoe on the ground and it unfolds into a spacious stable with a wide central aisle, stalls to accommodate up to eight horses, and sufficient feed and water to sustain the horses for 1 day. The stalls can house other quadrupedal mounts, but the stable provides only horse feed, which might be unsuitable for other creatures. As a 1-minute activity, which has the concentrate trait, you can alter the shape of the stalls to accommodate different mounts, though the space available within the stable never changes, only the layout. A metal horseshoe hangs inside the stable near the entrance. You can remove the horseshoe with an Interact action, which causes the stable to fold into the horseshoe, leaving it again looking as if it's made of worn wood.

>
[Canary](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2468)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 92

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Knowledge is often the key to a successful venture, and canaries are boots on the ground who can get the information you need to carry out your missions. Sometimes, you may need to gather information in an area or culture you're not familiar with, and you may need to do so without being seen or in advance of your arrival to that location. Utilizing a local network of eyes and ears is often the best way to carry out this type of reconnaissance. Organizations like the Firebrands have large networks of canaries scattered throughout the Inner Sea region capable of gathering information or following specific targets, and some Firebrands may even be canaries themselves.

 Discretion and confidentiality are two of the most important values for any member of a canary network. If an individual's identity or role is revealed, it can spell death—or worse—for them and the rest of the network. To help minimize this risk, canaries know only one or two other individuals within the network and never share the identities of others with their clients. In some cases, this network of informants may have two members residing in the same household without knowing that they're both involved. Due to this secretive nature, information must be passed securely— parchment slips baked into your bread or dropped into your pocket, a letter slipped under your door, a confirmation whispered into your ear.

 Canaries come in two varieties: informants and tails. A canary informant automatically [Aids](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) you on attempts to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) about a specific person, a locale, rumors spreading in the area, or movements of enemy forces, granting you a +1 circumstance bonus to your checks. Advanced canary informants critically succeed at Aiding you, granting you a +2 circumstance bonus to your check.

 Canary tails follow a specific individual. For each week that they are hired, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus on your check to Gather Information on the movements and mannerisms of the individual, up to a maximum of four weeks for a +4 bonus. After four weeks, the individual typically begins to suspect they are being tailed and shifts their schedule, limits their exposure, or otherwise changes their behavior to throw off any tails. The cost of this service increases over the weeks due to the increased risk posed to canaries by longer durations.

 The GM decides whether a canary network is in place for any given location and whether that network is able to collect the information needed to support you. In most cases, settlements of 5th level and higher have some kind of canary network in place; the network in a lower-level settlement might be sparser, requiring more time or higher payments, as determined by the GM. In some instances, canary networks might already know the exact information you are searching for and can provide the information forthright for the cost of one week of advanced services. For example, the network could already be keeping a list of corrupt bankers living in a specific city district and provide that information for 35 gp. The exact nature of each banker's corruption may be considered a different piece of information and require additional payments. Prices may be much higher for very specific information or information that took great effort for the network to acquire.

This blood-red candle is made from wax derived from oil shale found in certain parts of the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6). The wick burns with a flame that flickers and dances even if there's no draft to stir it. You activate the candle by lighting it, which causes creatures within 10 feet of the candle to find their emotions running high. Creatures in the area take a –1 status penalty to saving throws against [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60) effects. Once lit, the candle burns for 10 minutes. If extinguished, it can't be relit.

---

This golden candle bears the symbol of a specific deity emblazoned on its surface, surrounded by the iconography of that deity's faith. Once lit, this candle burns for 1 hour, and it can't be extinguished.

 Characters who cast divine spells and worship the deity emblazoned on the candle can perform their daily preparations within 10 feet of the lit candle to gain two additional spell slots for the day, each at half the highest spell slot they possess (for example, 4th-level slots if the caster can cast 8th-level spells). Prepared casters must prepare spells in these spell slots as they do for all their other spell slots.

 A caster's additional spell slots from the candle are lost the next time that caster performs their daily preparations. No one can benefit from more than one candle of invocation in a day, but multiple characters can benefit from a single candle's effects.

fields.text: Item 16 Candle of Invocation Uncommon Conjuration Consumable Divine Source Advanced Player's Guide pg. 256 Price 2,000 gp Usage held in 1 hand Activate Single Action Interact This golden candle bears the symbol of a specific deity emblazoned on its surface, surrounded by the iconography of that deity's faith. Once lit, this candle burns for 1 hour, and it can't be extinguished. Characters who cast divine spells and worship the deity emblazoned on the candle can perform their daily preparations within 10 feet of the lit candle to gain two additional spell slots for the day, each at half the highest spell slot they possess (for example, 4th-level slots if the caster can cast 8th-level spells). Prepared casters must prepare spells in these spell slots as they do for all their other spell slots. A caster's additional spell slots from the candle are lost the next time that caster performs their daily preparations. No one can benefit from more than one candle of invocation in a day, but multiple characters can benefit from a single candle's effects.

When lit, this black candle's eerie blue flame reveals the presence of invisible creatures. This tapered candle has a golden wick that burns with white fire. You activate the candle by lighting it, which causes creatures within 10 feet of the candle to find it difficult to tell falsehoods. Creatures in the area receive a –4 status penalty to Lie.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #162: Ruins of the Radiant Siege](/Sources.aspx?ID=54) pg. 73

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

A large crystal of [warpglass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=898) floats above the head of this silvery purple _+3 [anarchic](/Equipment.aspx?ID=290) [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2)_. If you successfully Strike a creature, the cane also affects the target with a [warpwave](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=82). While you carry the cane, you hear a constant, distracting chorus of laughing, incoherent [Protean](/Languages.aspx?ID=33) whispers and sing-song voices in your mind. Blatant acts of self-indulgence or narcissism quell these whispers, from a few minutes up to a full day depending on the scope of the act, but they immediately return when you use the artifact's powers. The gradually rising chorus eventually drives away rational thought and renders the cane's owner insane, even if staved off from time to time with self-centered acts. As the artifact's abilities pull material from the [Maelstrom](/Planes.aspx?ID=19), it doesn't function in areas where planar connections are severed.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;   **Trigger** You are targeted by a ranged attack from an opponent you can see;  **Effect** You draw a temporary shield of chaotic turbulence with a cerulean flash. You gain a +3 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (command, envision, Interact);     **Effect** The _Cane of the Maelstrom_ casts a 5th-level [_hallucinatory terrain_](/Spells.aspx?ID=145) spell and infuses the illusion with quasi-real substance drawn from the primal chaos of the Maelstrom. Creatures that don't disbelieve the illusion treat structures and terrain created through the spell as though they were real, ascending illusory stairs, becoming trapped by illusory quicksand, and so on. If no creature disbelieves the illusion during its duration, the changes become wholly real and permanent when its duration expires.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (Interact);     **Effect** The _Cane of the Maelstrom_ casts a 5th-level [_creation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=54) spell, except the duration is unlimited and you can create delicate or complex objects by succeeding at an applicable [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) skill check when you activate this ability.

**Destruction** Trapping a lawful demigod in the _hallucinatory terrain_ created by the cane and leaving it imprisoned for a year and a day causes a deific overload that destroys the artifact. When the artifact is destroyed, the terrain imprisoning the demigod crumbles away and the demigod is freed.

---

This suit of _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804)[ assisting](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1829) [leaf weave](/Armor.aspx?ID=28)_ is composed entirely of primal-infused leaves bestowed by a dying [arboreal](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=364). The leaves display the vibrant greens of summer, as if full of life, regardless of the time that has passed since the arboreal gifted them. The armor is constantly drawing in imperceptible amounts of primal energy to help bear its wearer’s burdens. You can draw deeply upon the untapped reserves of primal magic within it and infuse yourself with these energies to a limited extent, giving you a burst of quickness.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1470), envision **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_haste_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1553) targeting yourself. In addition to the effects of the spell, visible primal energy surges over the armor for the duration. This has no mechanical impact.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include leaves freely given by an arboreal.

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 181

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

In an effort to spread the knowledge of magic as widely as possible, worshippers of [Nethys](/Deities.aspx?ID=12) discovered a way to bind cantrips into cards accessible even to non-spellcasters. The deck contains thick parchment cards, each roughly half the size of a playing card. In precise, no-nonsense script, each card simply states the name of its cantrip, color-coded based on its school.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action or more Actions" /> (envision, Interact);     **Effect** You envision your desired cantrip, causing its card to rise to the top of the deck, and draw the card. The deck casts that cantrip as a 1st-level spell, with a DC of 15 and a spell attack modifier of +5. The card crumbles into dust as the cantrip takes effect. The activation takes the same number of actions as the cantrip you chose takes to cast.

---

This regal blue cape is crafted from a hefty yet elegant velvet embroidered with ornate silver stars and dragons. Falling in a cascade of fabric, the cape rustles and flows in all the right ways and hangs upon your shoulders in a way that flatters your form and figure. You draw the eyes of those around you and gain a +2 item bonus to your [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** With a flourish of your cape, you make a grand entrance that draws the attention of those around you. You cast [_enthrall_](/Spells.aspx?ID=104) with a DC of 25. The spell gains the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) trait and loses the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait. You Sustain the Spell by continuing to sweep the cape about.

May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts **Source** [Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was](/Sources.aspx?ID=214) pg. 81 **Price** 100 gp **Usage** worn cloak **Bulk** L --- While [Yaezhing](/Deities.aspx?ID=184) is feared and seldom worshipped in the open, some regions of Tian Xia see him as a god of necessary evil and their only hope for justice. This garment is often worn by bounty hunters or priests of Yaezhing, yet non-worshippers of the god of harsh justice sometimes wear this item without fear of religious persecution. The red cape appears almost black while in the shadows, with a lighter red mandala pattern on it that resembles a shuriken. When you invest a _cape of justice_, you must designate a single creature as your offender. You must have met the creature before, or the creature should have a persona well known to the public (for instance, a bandit's epithet, if not their face as shown on a wanted poster). You gain a +1 item bonus to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) this creature. If you don't designate a creature as your offender when you invest the _cape of justice_, or if 24 hours pass without you either slaying or capturing your offender, your thoughts become worried and distracted and you take a –1 item penalty to Perception checks for the next 24 hours. **Activate** command, Interact ([force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** By using a free hand to grab the edge of your cape and give it a quick flourish, you cause a red, shuriken-shaped bolt of force to fire at a target within 60 feet that you can see. This bright red-and-gold cape is often interlaced with glittery threads and serves as a distraction. While wearing the cape, you gain a +2 item bonus to Deception checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_dimension door_](/Spells.aspx?ID=69). The space you leave and the one you appear in are filled with puffs of smoke that make anyone within concealed until they leave the smoke or the end of your next turn, at which point the smoke dissipates. Strong winds immediately disperse the smoke.

[Cape of the Open Sky](/Equipment.aspx?ID=948)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Fists of the Ruby Phoenix</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #167: Ready? Fight!](/Sources.aspx?ID=86) pg. 74

**Price** 22,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This cloth of gold cape was originally gifted to one of Goka's emperors centuries ago. Since then, it has spawned many imitations, which are all alike in that they are dyed with an elaborate seal depicting two drakes flanking Goka's palace and the Seven Dragons Bridge. The beautiful cape grants you a +3 item bonus to checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) and to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50). While you wear the cape, the weather (including wind and fog) doesn't affect your movement or vision. Additionally, whenever you fall while wearing the _cape of the open sky_, the cape automatically casts [_feather fall_](/Spells.aspx?ID=111) on you.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** The cape becomes a pair of golden drake wings that grant you a fly Speed of 30 feet for 1 hour.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** The cloak pushes you onward. You Stride or [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) up to your Speed, but you can move only in a straight line. You gain a +15-foot status bonus to your Speed and fly Speed for this movement.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    pfs="Limited"
>
[Capsaicin Tonic](/Equipment.aspx?ID=903)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Troubles in Otari</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=59" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Troubles in Otari](/Sources.aspx?ID=55) pg. 60, [A Few Flowers More](/Sources.aspx?ID=202) pg. 13

**Price** 17 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This translucent, pale-yellow drink has several pepper seeds suspended within it. Although the tonic is painfully spicy when first consumed, the heat soon fades as the tonic coats your throat. In the next hour, you can use the activation below up to three times; the third time you use it, the effects of the capsaicin tonic end. While under the effects of the tonic, you can easily consume even the spiciest of foods without trouble.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You belch out a foul-smelling cloud of blisteringly spicy gas that fills a single square adjacent to you. Creatures within the cloud are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4), and all creatures outside the cloud are concealed to creatures within it. The cloud remains for 1 minute but can be dispersed by a strong wind. The cloud deals 1d4 fire damage to creatures that enter the cloud on their turn, as well as to creatures that start their turn in the cloud (a creature takes this damage no more than once per round, even if it moves back and forth into the cloud multiple times during the round).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Captivating Bauble](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2098)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=60" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=101" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=163" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 92

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Three Actions" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

**Requirement** You are a master in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6).
</row>

</column>

---

This talisman appears as an ornate piece of jewelry of the highest quality. When you Activate it, your speech and mannerisms become supernaturally compelling for up to 1 hour. By engaging an intelligent creature in conversation for at least 1 minute, you can cause them to become [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14) unless they succeed at a DC 30 Will save. This fascination lasts for as long as you continue conversing or until you move at least 20 feet away. When the effect ends, the target becomes temporarily immune for 24 hours. If you or any ally within 120 feet takes an overtly [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) while a creature is fascinated by the bauble, the bauble burns out in a shower of sparks and all its effects end.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

By engaging an intelligent creature in conversation for at least 1 minute, you can cause them to become [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) unless they succeed at a DC 30 Will save. This fascination lasts for as long as you continue conversing or until you move at least 20 feet away. When the effect ends, the target becomes temporarily immune for 24 hours. **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 200 **Price** 10 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand --- Named because of its popularity among thieves to distract any authorities in pursuit, a captivating rosebud has a near-irresistible fragrance. **Activate—Scent of Roses** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=246)) **Effect** You throw the _captivating rosebud_ in a square adjacent to you. The rosebud quickly sprouts into a little rosebush that lasts for 1 hour. Any creature that passes within 15 feet of the rose bush, other than yourself, must attempt a DC 18 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes a –1 status penalty to Perception checks for 10 minutes.
**Failure** As success, but a –2 penalty.
**Critical Failure** As success, but a –2 penalty and the creature is [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14) by the rosebush. **Activate—Rose Vines** 10 minutes ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Effect** You plant the _captivating rosebud_ into a square adjacent to a building or other structure. It grows into a rosebush that stretches up to 30 feet tall. You and your allies can use the rosebush as a ladder to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) easily up and down the side of the adjacent structure, but all other creatures must succeed at a DC 17 Will saving throw or fail to notice the rosebush's presence.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 84 **Price** 250 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Activate**([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) --- A _captivating score_ is a piece of parchment prepared for musical notation, long enough for a short song. You must be trained in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) to properly compose this missive (or trained in an appropriate [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill your GM allows). You choose one of the emotions described below and write a musical composition to convey that emotion about a subject of your choice, typically a person or group. When activated, the missive plays a note-perfect rendition of the inscribed score. Each creature that can hear the score must succeed at a DC 28 Will save or be influenced to feel the emotion you chose toward the subject of your composition. This lasts for 1 hour, typically returning the creature to its initial attitude unless new events have altered their attitude long-term.
  • **Positive** Your song engenders sympathy, adoration, joy, or a similar emotion. An affected creature's attitude toward the subject improves by one step, such as from [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=25) to [friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18).
  • **Negative** Your song spurs anger, sadness, jealousy, or a similar emotion. An affected creature's attitude toward the subject worsens by one step, such as from indifferent to [unfriendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=40).
When composing this missive, you can add a small notation or illustration of a type of instrument. If you do, the music sounds like that instrument, and if you didn't specify, it sounds vaguely like a recorder. The choice of a louder instrument doesn't make the music carry farther.

Sometimes called liquid persuasion, this sweet-tasting tincture induces euphoria that lowers inhibitions and increases trust. This +[3](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [extending](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2836) [urumi](/Weapons.aspx?ID=306) was fashioned after the legendary eightheaded orochi serpent, with its whiplike metal blades carved to resemble the many heads of the mythical beast, and its hilt wrapped in scaled leather. These weapons are commonly used by those who worship an orochi, raiding and threatening settlements to obtain sacrifices for the beast in hopes of being granted some modicum of its power. 

**Activate—Serpent’s Kiss** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You use your urumi as an effigy with which to call upon an [orochi](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1416)’s power, offering your blood in exchange. You can make up to eight [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) with a –2 penalty, each against a different target within 30 feet. For each Strike you choose to make, you take 1d6 piercing damage. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don’t increase your penalty until you’ve made all your attacks.

fields.text: Item 18 Caress of the Great Serpent Uncommon Magical Source Tian Xia Character Guide pg. 126 Price 24,000 gp Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 2 Base Weapon Urumi This +3 greater striking extending urumi was fashioned after the legendary eightheaded orochi serpent, with its whiplike metal blades carved to resemble the many heads of the mythical beast, and its hilt wrapped in scaled leather. These weapons are commonly used by those who worship an orochi, raiding and threatening settlements to obtain sacrifices for the beast in hopes of being granted some modicum of its power. Activate—Serpent’s Kiss Three Actions (concentrate) Frequency once per day; Effect You use your urumi as an effigy with which to call upon an orochi’s power, offering your blood in exchange. You can make up to eight Strikes with a –2 penalty, each against a different target within 30 feet. For each Strike you choose to make, you take 1d6 piercing damage. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don’t increase your penalty until you’ve made all your attacks.

>
[Carrion Cask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1797)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 178

**Price** 500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Characters from Geb have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This stylized, palm-sized box contains a black, ooze-like substance that can easily devour a corpse in moments, breaking the body down into a necromantic sludge.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You feed a corpse of a Small-sized or larger creature to the cask, little by little. The activation requires a three-action activity for a Small or Medium creature, a 1-minute activity for a Larger creature, and a 10-minute activity for a Huge creature. A Gargantuan creature is too large for the cask to devour.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** The _carrion cask_ has consumed a corpse since the last time it was activated; **Effect** You release the sludge from the _carrion cask's_ last meal in a pulse of necromantic energy. Creatures in a 30-foot cone take 6d6 negative damage, with a DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Carver-Cutter](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2640)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 201

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Battle Axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=16)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Many of the experienced woodcarvers of the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) learn to fight as well, the better to travel into hazardous areas in search of rare and beautiful types of wood for their craft. A _carver-cutter_ serves a dual role as a weapon and a tool for felling trees and engraving wood. The _+2 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [battle axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=16)_ looks like an exquisitely made woodcutting axe.

**Activate—Carving Chisel** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You pull free a woodworking chisel stored in the knob of the axe. It can have any standard chisel shape you imagine as you activate this ability. You get a +2 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks for woodworking if you use chisels from the _carver-cutter_. The chisel also functions as a [main-gauche](/Weapons.aspx?ID=32). All runes on the axe are replicated on the chisel, but only while both items are on the same person. You can Interact to reinsert the chisel.

**Activate—Chop Down** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** Make a Strike with the axe against a [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) creature or a creature made primarily of wood. This Strike deals an additional 2d6 precision damage, and on a hit, the creature is [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) for 1 minute.

Each _cassock of devotion_ depicts scenes related to the domains of a certain deity. It serves as a religious symbol of that deity, and it doesn’t need to be wielded to provide that benefit. >
[Castrovel's Beacon](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3688)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 77

**Price** 4,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The tip of this _[+2 greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [brilliant](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2833) standard-grade [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) [rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=391)_ shines with a flickering sheen of green light that mimics the glittering appearance of Castrovel in the night sky. The carrier of _Castrovel’s Beacon_ instinctively knows Castrovel’s position in the sky even if it hasn’t actually yet risen into view, which grants the wielder a +2 item bonus to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=2406) when using the stars to orient themself. Additionally, the weapon grants a +2 item bonus to all saving throws against effects that cause the [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) or [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) conditions.

When its _brilliant_ rune is activated, the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) rank is 6 and the counteract modifier is +21.

**Activate—Starlight Burst** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_vibrant pattern_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1741) from _Castrovel’s Beacon_ as a 6th-rank [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) spell with a DC 31 Will save. Creatures with the [elf](/Traits.aspx?ID=588) trait are immune to Starlight Burst, and creatures with the [demon](/Traits.aspx?ID=573) trait take a –2 item penalty on all Will saves against the effect.

fields.text: Item 14 Castrovel's Beacon May contain spoilers from Spore War Unique Magical Source Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt pg. 77 Price 4,500 gp Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 1 The tip of this +2 greater striking brilliant standard-grade cold iron rapier shines with a flickering sheen of green light that mimics the glittering appearance of Castrovel in the night sky. The carrier of Castrovel’s Beacon instinctively knows Castrovel’s position in the sky even if it hasn’t actually yet risen into view, which grants the wielder a +2 item bonus to Sense Direction when using the stars to orient themself. Additionally, the weapon grants a +2 item bonus to all saving throws against effects that cause the dazzled or blinded conditions. When its brilliant rune is activated, the counteract rank is 6 and the counteract modifier is +21. Activate—Starlight Burst Two Actions (manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect You cast vibrant pattern from Castrovel’s Beacon as a 6th-rank arcane spell with a DC 31 Will save. Creatures with the elf trait are immune to Starlight Burst, and creatures with the demon trait take a –2 item penalty on all Will saves against the effect.

The Galtan orange cat was bred to have short legs and a thick orange coat so it could easily hunt vermin in tight spaces. They were often kept as staff in noble houses. During the Galtan revolution, as noble households fell, these cats were left to fend for their themselves. While there's a substantial feral population, only one breeder of pedigreed Galtan orange cats remains, making them highly sought after.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=589" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 246, [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 286

**Price** 7 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

After you consume this elixir, your vision sharpens and you become sensitive to even the most minute movements. For the next minute, you reduce the flat check to target [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) creatures to 5, and you don't need to attempt a flat check to target [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) creatures. These benefits apply only against creatures within 30 feet of you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 0+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Catch Pole](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3245)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 112

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This sturdy pole has a rope attached to one end in a loop with the other end extending to the handle. You can pull the handle side of the rope to tighten the loop. Using this loop, you can [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) without having a free hand. A creature grappled this way receives a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls when [Striking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with an unarmed attack. Due to limitations in the size of the loop, a catch pole can only be used on creatures sized Medium or smaller.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</traits>

**Price** 2 gp

<row gap="medium">

</column>

Giant Catch Pole
</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 112

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Bulk** 2

</row>

</column>

---

A giant catch pole is made from thicker steel and heavier rope. It functions the same as a catch pole but can be used to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) creatures up to your normal size limit. However, the implement is so ungainly that you are [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) while wielding it.

<title

>
Superior Catch Pole
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Bulk** 1

</row>

</column>

---

A superior catch pole has a pole made of dawnsilver, and the loop at the end is silk rope, making it sturdier and more agile. It functions the same as a catch pole but gives you a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks made to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) with it.

>
[Cauldron of Nightmares](/Equipment.aspx?ID=891)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #161: Belly of the Black Whale](/Sources.aspx?ID=51) pg. 78

**Price** 13,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Engraved with carvings of tortured souls, this green cauldron has two abilities that allow it to capture nightmares and then unleash them on the world. The cauldron has an affinity for preying on the minds of captives and prisoners, who take a –2 circumstance penalty to saving throws against it. Good creatures are [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) while carrying, wielding, or wearing this item crafted by the sea-witches.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact ([divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The cauldron casts [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=208) (DC 35) on a target creature that you know by name. The target must be on the same plane as you. If the target fails its save and is 15th level or lower, you add its nightmare to the cauldron. The cauldron can hold only six nightmares at a time; when you add a new nightmare, you choose which six to keep.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You spill the nightmarish contents of the cauldron onto the ground and choose one creature whose nightmare is stored in your cauldron. A nightmare copy of the chosen creature springs to life from the bubbling pile of horror. The cauldron casts [_duplicate foe_](/Spells.aspx?ID=93) on the target, ignoring the range restriction, and the target automatically fails its saving throw. All enemies within 20 feet of the cauldron are subjected to a [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68) spell (DC 35). All other nightmares stored in the cauldron are lost. The cauldron becomes totally inert and can't be used again for 1 week.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=208).

</column>

Contained in a specially enchanted small leather or hide sack, _deteriorating dust_ is a potent caustic agent and a prized item among Rovagug’s more discreet followers.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You sprinkle the _deteriorating dust_ over an unattended Medium or smaller object. The dust quickly fades to a transparent color and the object immediately begins to rust, melt, or otherwise fall apart. For the listed time, the object takes constant damage; if the object has a Hardness, then the dust gradually reduces the object’s Hardness instead. If the _deteriorating dust_ is still active after the object’s Hardness is reduced to 0, it deals damage to the object as previously described. If the object survives, reduced Hardness returns after the dust’s duration expires, but any damage remains.

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 105 **Price** 2,600 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands **Bulk** 2 --- The main portion of this set of bagpipes is fashioned from the dried skin of a [cauthooj](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2870), with the feathers still attached. The bird’s vocal cords are crafted into the instrument’s reeds. The pipes grant a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks while playing music with them. **Activate—Disorienting Fugue** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You play several notes on the pipes, quickly altering their pitch and tone. Each creature within a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) must attempt a DC 31 Will save to resist the song. Creatures that attempt this save become temporarily immune to Disorienting Fugue for 1 minute. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected and its temporary immunity to Disorienting Fugue increases to 1 hour.
**Success** The target is unaffected.
**Failure** The target is [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The target is confused for 1 round and immediately attacks itself (in the normal fashion for attacking oneself while confused). This [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) doesn’t give the creature a flat check to recover from the confusion. **Activate—Throw Song** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet attempts a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against you or an ally; **Effect** You let loose a staccato chirp from the pipes that appears to come from somewhere else. The triggering creature must attempt a DC 31 Will save. On a failure, the creature redirects the Strike to another creature of your choice within reach of the melee Strike. If no other creatures are within range, the affected creature instead takes a –2 penalty to the Strike. **Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the skin and vocal cords of a [cauthooj](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2870).

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands](/Sources.aspx?ID=33) pg. 75

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>1 minute (Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Cave worm repellent is a highly noxious oil that can be applied to a creature or sprinkled in a circle around a 10-foot-radius area. In either case, after it is applied, it lasts for 24 hours or until it is scrubbed clean with 1 minute of work.

 When applied to a creature, the repellent causes [cave worms](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=21) of the indicated type to avoid attacking that creature in melee as long as they have something else nearby to attack. The repellent does not deter a cave worm from making ranged attacks against a coated target. If no creatures are within a cave worm's reach and it wants to approach and make a melee attack, it approaches and attacks a non-coated creature if it can without spending more actions to do so. 

If the coated creature is swallowed by the designated type of cave worm, the cave worm must succeed at a Fortitude save or involuntarily regurgitate the swallowed creature on the next round (a single action).

 When sprinkled around an area, cave worm repellent negates any chance of a random encounter with the particular type of cave worm in that area, as the creatures purposefully avoid the affected area.

 Other types of repellent that function similarly to this one might exist at the GM's discretion. Uncommon or rare creatures are typically much harder to repel, and repellent against them might necessitate harvesting ingredients from the creatures themselves (such as the creature's liver or a certain gland).

Usage etched onto medium or heavy armor This armor can channel your life force into an enhanced [_wall of stone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=365).

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** By stamping your foot on the ground and calling out to spirits of stone, you summon a stone wall. The effect is dismissed if you move more than 30 feet away from the stone wall or if you spend a single action with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.

---

This suit of _+2 resilient [chain mail](/Armor.aspx?ID=9)_ is made of fine white links of a strange and slightly translucent pale metal, and the sleeves and skirt are fashioned into smaller trails that resemble feathers. Unlike normal chain mail, celestial armor has no Speed reduction, its armor check penalty is 0, and its Bulk is 1. 

 You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws against fiends. You appear radiant while you wear the armor, giving you a +2 item bonus to Diplomacy checks against all creatures except fiends.

 If you are not good, you are drained 2 while wearing _celestial armor_. You can’t recover from this condition while wearing the armor.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The armor sprouts glowing wings that grant you a fly Speed of 30 feet. The wings shed bright light in a 40-foot radius (and dim light to the next 40 feet). The wings fade away after 10 minutes.

**Craft Requirements** You are good.

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

From blade to pommel, this sword is carved from a branch of the now-extinct celestial peach tree. The blade of this _+3 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [disrupting](/Equipment.aspx?ID=294) [holy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=299) [peachwood](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1543) [shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43)_ has ancient runes that can permanently destroy the most powerful [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160)—if you are willing to pay the price. An undead creature of 12th level or lower that takes damage from a Strike with the sword takes 10d6 positive damage (DC 35 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=326) Fortitude save). This damage is separate from the Strike itself and isn't included in any effect based on the Strike's damage.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;   **Trigger** You critically hit an undead creature with the _celestial peachwood sword_; **Requirements** once per day; **Effect** The creature must succeed at a DC 35 Fortitude save or be destroyed. If the undead fails its saving throw and is destroyed, you suffer a backlash, taking 1d6 negative damage per level of the destroyed undead.

---

This _[+1 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [spiked chain](/Weapons.aspx?ID=417)_, strung with bloodied military insignia and other grisly trophies harvested from slain soldiers, is commonly used by [hobgoblin](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=78) commandants to motivate their troops. On a critical hit, the chain of command deals an additional 1d6 mental damage.

**Activate—Mercy of the Commander** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))   **Requirements** Your last action was a critical hit with the _chain of command_; **Effect** The _chain of command_ gains the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) trait for 1 minute.

**Activate—Will of the Commander** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** You cast [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1470) on the target of your critical hit with a DC of 22. Regardless of the outcome, the target is then immune to this effect for 24 hours.

**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of _command_.

</title>

<traits>
